items.title: Puppet report-processing deserialization bug (CVSS 9.4) is now in CISA KEV as attackers exploit it
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731, an untrusted-deserialization flaw in Puppet's report handling that yields remote code execution, to KEV on November 17, with a December 1 federal deadline; no attack details have been shared. Exploitation needs a valid CA-signed agent certificate, so servers that auto-sign agent requests are most exposed, and a companion bug (CVE-2026-115732, CVSS 9.0) bypasses certificate-name authorization in Puppet and OpenVox. Upgrade to Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 (Core 9.1.3 / 8.22.2) or the fixed OpenVox agent and server builds, tighten CA auto-signing, and check Puppet servers for compromise, since stolen CA keys would let an attacker impersonate managed hosts.

items.title: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is under active attack, and the September fix missed versions 4.0.0-6.1.4
items.summary: The Apache Software Foundation says CVE-2026-129448, an unauthenticated deserialization bug in Roller's XML-RPC endpoint, is being actively exploited; the endpoint unpacks vendor extension types before checking who is calling. It is the same flaw as September's CVE-2026-82384, which was scoped only to 6.1.5, and covers Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later; if you cannot, set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping and restart, because switching XML-RPC off in the admin UI does not stop older builds from deserializing the request.

items.title: CISA KEV adds Synology DSM, LiteLLM guardrail sandbox escape, end-of-life Apache Axis 1.x and REDCap bugs
items.summary: CISA's November 18 KEV update covers an unauthenticated RCE in Synology DSM and BeeStation OS, a LiteLLM proxy bug where an authenticated user can escape the AST sandbox on the /guardrails/test_custom_code route, an unsafe-reflection RCE in Apache Axis 1.x triggered by a crafted SOAP Fault, and a REDCap code-injection flaw reachable with a public survey hash. Federal deadlines are November 21 for three of them and December 2 for LiteLLM. Patch DSM and REDCap to the fixed builds, run a LiteLLM build newer than April 8, 2026 and keep its admin routes off the internet, and plan to migrate off Axis 1.x, which is end-of-life and fixed only by an upstream commit.

items.title: 'nginx2root': public PoCs for a 10-year-old NGINX HTTP/2 bug show worker RCE, chained to host root via a kernel flaw
items.summary: F5 fixed five NGINX flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, led by CVE-2026-123007, an HTTP/2 flow-control error present since 1.9.5 in 2015; Rapid7, Wiz and Xint have published proof-of-concept code, and Xint chained it with a Linux SCTP kernel bug to reach root on cloud hosts. No in-the-wild exploitation is reported yet, and the attacks need ASLR bypassed, AVX-512 CPUs and sustained heavy HTTP/2 traffic. Upgrade to NGINX 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 (Plus 37.3.0.1 or 37.0.8.1) with a full restart rather than a reload, check distro packages separately, disable HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 if patching must wait, and block the sctp module where it is not needed.

items.title: F5 ships hotfix-only patches for six critical BIG-IP data-plane overflows tied to specific iRule and APM setups
items.summary: Six unauthenticated stack overflows in BIG-IP's traffic microkernel can crash TMM and may allow code execution when a virtual server uses certain features, such as iRules calling PEM::subscriber, MR::message route, PSC::ip_address, GENERICMESSAGE::route or DNS::scrape, or an APM per-request policy with the Client Information and Endpoint Security agents. None is reported exploited, but fixes exist only as engineering hotfixes and there is no workaround. Audit virtual servers for those configurations, request and install the matching EHF for BIG-IP, BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes or CNF, and apply the regular releases that fix the lower-rated iControl and SAML bugs in the same batch.

items.title: PHP Foundation pre-announces a critical security release for November 19, 14:00-14:30 UTC
items.summary: The PHP Foundation says releases due Thursday fix bugs rated critical, though they need non-default configurations or uncommon setups. One is CVE-2026-115560, a session RCE that requires the serialize handler to be switched to 'php' at runtime with ini_set() before session_start() while session upload progress is enabled. Schedule the upgrade for as soon as the builds land, and until then set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and check whether any app changes session.serialize_handler at runtime.

items.title: 'Trigram' fakes about 50 AI and crypto brands to get developers to run infostealers, using a forged commit and an IDE extension
items.summary: Stormshield tracks Trigram, which it links with high confidence to the UNK_DeadDrop cluster, as luring developers with fake job, conference and parcel sites that ask them to paste a 'technical check' command; the loader installs Node.js and runs an encrypted stealer in memory that takes browser data, wallets, SSH keys and .env files, then adds the Overlord RAT. Other routes include a forged October 31 commit to the antd-img-crop GitHub repo that adds a prebuild.js hook (the npm package was not touched) and a sideloaded VS Code/Cursor extension named google-dev-tools.google-update-support. Treat 'run this command' steps in hiring or event flows as hostile, review build hooks in cloned repos, and allow-list IDE extensions.

items.title: Canonical opens an opt-in 'Edge' archive of AI-agent-written Ubuntu security backports, released before human review
items.summary: Ubuntu Pro customers can now opt in to patches from Surge, a chain of agents that matches vulnerability reports to Ubuntu packages, pulls the upstream fix, has several models write competing backports and lets a panel of judge models pick one, escalating to a human only on deadlock or low confidence. Patches still go through Ubuntu's deterministic build tests, cover known userspace flaws only, and leave out the kernel, which moves to a two-week SRU cycle. Leave Edge off for production unless you can test the patches yourself, since enabling it moves the job of judging patch safety from Canonical to you.

items.title: Arize Phoenix CVSS 10 flaw lets an unauthenticated GraphQL call leak env vars and PHOENIX_SECRET via chat templates
items.summary: In the Arize Phoenix LLM observability platform, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passes attacker-supplied f-string templates to a formatter that does not block private attributes, so a crafted field can walk Python internals and read environment variables and module state. Leaking PHOENIX_SECRET would let an attacker forge admin sessions and decrypt stored credentials, and the endpoint needs no login on default installs. Rapid7 lists versions from 13.0.0 as affected and 15.7.0 as the fix; upgrade to the current release, keep Phoenix off the public internet, and rotate PHOENIX_SECRET and stored provider keys if it was exposed.

items.title: macOS 27.3 beta splits broad Mac permissions into narrower grants as Apple reacts to AI agents taking control of desktops
items.summary: Apple is splitting the old Device Control and Data Access permission into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility, scoping Full Disk Access to chosen folders, offering an ask-every-time option, and showing an indicator when one app drives another. Apple ties the change to the risk of handing agent apps whole-Mac access; existing grants stay in place for now. Developers of agent and automation tools should handle folder-limited access in onboarding and apply for entitlements where needed, and Mac admins should review which apps hold broad grants.
